articles.title_en: ‘Even its loos are on the outside’: hi-tech, inside-out marvel the Lloyd’s building i
articles.title_ru: ‘Even its loos are on the outside’: hi-tech, inside-out marvel the Lloyd’s building i
articles.preview_en: It has been likened to a monster, an oil rig – and the Parthenon.
articles.preview_ru: It has been likened to a monster, an oil rig – and the Parthenon.
articles.full_en: It has been likened to a monster, an oil rig – and the Parthenon. Now, for its 40th birthday, the astonishing London landmark has joined the Open House festival, to grant admirers a rare look around the inside In his 2012 book A New Kind of Bleak, the critic Owen Hatherley called it “monstrous, compelling” and utterly messed-up. Back in the 1980s, a then Prince Charles suggested it had been inspired by a North Sea oil rig. But none of this stopped it from becoming, in 2011, the youngest ever building to be given Grade I-listed status in the UK. And now, as part of its 40th anniversary celebrations, the Lloyd’s building will open to the public for the first time since 2014 for one day only during London’s Open House festival. The iconic building in the heart of the financial district was designed by architect Richard Rogers to house the global insurance marketplace. Its futuristic facade has been a celebrated part of the City of London skyline since it opened in 1986, but the interior is rarely seen by the public.
